newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia government and Howard widen lead in poll.
newsitem.headline: Australia government and Howard widen lead in poll.

text.p: Australia's conservative government and prime minister have widened their poll lead over the Labor opposition and its leader, a newspaper poll published on Tuesday showed.

The Liberal-National government's popularity remained steady at 42 percent over the past two weeks, while Labor's support fell to 36 percent from 40 percent, according to the latest Newspoll in The Australian newspaper.
Prime Minister John Howard's rating as preferred prime minister fell one point to 43 percent, while opposition leader Kim Beazley's fell two points to 29 percent.
But 28 percent of those surveyed remained uncommitted on the preferred prime minister question.

Importantly for the government, the level of satisfaction with Howard's performance increased four points to 44 percent, while dissatisfaction fell three points to 45 percent since the last poll two weeks ago.
The latest result is a marked change in Howard's ranking after several months where his dissatisfaction rating has heavily outweighed his satisfaction rating.

The turnaround in Howard's rating by the electorate also comes after a survey of voter attitudes showed widespread dissatisfaction with Howard's leadership performance, including from among Liberal supporters.
The poll also showed a one point increase in support for race row politician Pauline Hanson, whose One Nation Party increased to seven percent.
One Nation is still well ahead of the traditional third force in Australian politics, the Australian Democrats.
Democrats support increased one point to five percent.

The latest Newspoll measure of primary support compared with the government's primary vote of 47.3 percent and Labor's 38.8 percent in the March 1996 election that saw Howard sweep into office and end 13 years of Labor rule.
The latest Newspoll surveyed 1,139 voters by telephone around the country over the last weekend.
